channel.title: aibek.
channel.description: product designer in Talas. making apps that work on a cheap phone and a slow network. writing sometimes.

item.title: What I'd tell a design student in Talas
item.description: Go to the bazaar and watch how people use their phones. Then design. Your user's phone is older and slower than yours. Always. Write in Iradi first, translate to English second, and check that the Russian fits on the button. Make something small for someone you know. It will teach you more than a…

item.title: Twenty years of Kündölük comments
item.description: I found my old comments on Bekzhan's 2005 blog. "does it play mp3??" on a gadget blog. "the atm at bereke ate my card, it was you??". "brat i read all the blog again today". Everything I know about writing for real people I learned in those comment boxes: short, specific, kind, a bit rude. That is…

item.title: A bus timetable for the village
item.description: [photo: bus | The village bus at the final stop.] Side project: a timetable page for one village bus line, made with the driver. He doesn't use apps. So the page is one screen, big numbers, works without data once loaded, and the driver can change the times by sending a text message to a number.…

item.title: Iradi letters on small screens
item.description: Iradi has ü, ö, ı, ñ, ş, ç, ğ. On a small screen the dots and the cedilla disappear in the wrong font. We tested twelve fonts at 14 px on that bazaar phone. Four passed. The winner is boring, which in type is a compliment. Also: "ı" without the dot is a different letter. If your font draws it with…

item.title: Designing for the slow evening
item.description: [photo: night | Talas at 9 p.m., when every flat is on the same network.] Every app I design is tested at 9 p.m., not 9 a.m. In the evening the network in Talas is full and every screen loads twice as slowly. So: Text first, pictures later. The user can start reading while the photo is still…

item.title: Finally a blog
item.description: Bekzhan wrote in 2013 that "Aibek never wrote". Ten years later: fine. Here I am, on the same Kündölük, with the new Bento theme. This page is a grid of boxes because that is what designers' sites look like in 2023. I know. I like boxes.
